punchline: Anxious and avoidant people are drawn to each other, and the pull they feel is part of the trap.
thirty_sec: In Attached, Levine and Heller describe a pairing they call the anxious-avoidant trap. The anxious partner calls and texts to get closer. The avoidant partner hears pressure and pulls away, asking for space or fixating on small flaws. Each move sets off the other's, and each person blames the other. The authors say nobody is the villain, and once you can see the loop you can change your own half, for instance by waiting an hour before the next message.
